THIS CRIMINAL MISC. CASE HAVING COME UP FOR ADMISSION ON 09.10.2024, THE COURT ON THE SAME DAY PASSED THE FOLLOWING:
 2024:KER:75079 Crl.M.C.No.8324 of 2024  -:2:-
 BECHU KURIAN THOMAS, J.

ORDER Petitioner is the 8th accused in Crime No.680/2024 of Anchal Police Station, alleging offences punishable under Sections 420, 468, 471 and 406 r/w Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.
2.

According to the prosecution, accused 1 to 8 had, in furtherance of their common intention to cause wrongful gain to themselves and wrongful loss to the defacto complainant, made the defacto complainant believe that the first accused is the owner of the vehicle bearing registration No.KL-13-AE-7000 and sold it to him by forging agreements in the name of the petitioner and obtained Rs.35,00,000/- as consideration for the same, and thereafter, on coming to know about it,
the petitioner-8th accused filed a complaint against the other accused and the third respondent,
alleging loss of Rs.50,00,000/-, and the accused committed the offences as alleged.
3.

Sri. P.V.Anoop, the learned counsel for the petitioner, submitted that the uncontroverted allegations in the FIR cannot implicate the petitioner as an accused, and therefore, proceedings against him are liable to be quashed.

4. Sri. Noushad.K.A, the learned Public Prosecutor, however, 2024:KER:75079 submitted that it is too premature a stage to quash the proceedings since the involvement of the petitioner in the crime has to be thoroughly investigated.
5. Having considered the rival contentions and noticing that the FIR was registered only on 08.06.2024, I am of the view that this is too premature a stage to quash the proceedings.
The involvement of the petitioner is specifically alleged in the FIR.
Therefore, it cannot be stated that the uncontroverted allegations do not make out any of the offences.
It is also noticed that petitioner had handed over the vehicle under an agreement to other accused, who, after several months, is alleged to have transferred the vehicle to the defacto complainant.
The question whether the aforesaid act was done with an intention to cheat a person, will have to be investigated.
In such circumstances, I am of the view that this is not a fit case to interfere under Section 528 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023.
